alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have simply misheard and repeated back partial figures without intending to skip verification — a transcription/audio artifact rather than a rep choice.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pin down one clear bill number before moving on — repeat it back once and confirm ('so around $150 a month, is that right?') rather than letting three different figures pass without resolution.

stewart_read: Customer discloses a job-loss/financial-hardship situation unprompted while explaining the credit issue. The rep's next line moves straight into asking for the score number with no acknowledgment of the hardship.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this was purely informational (explaining why credit is low) rather than an emotional disclosure needing a response, since the customer's tone stayed practical rather than distressed.
coaching_implication: Even a brief acknowledgment ('sorry to hear that, glad you're back on your feet') costs nothing and matches Ion's own philosophy on vulnerability disclosures. Coach the rep to build in a one-line human acknowledgment before continuing the qualifier.

quote: Okay. Well, yeah. I would just recommend looking into solar once that is above $6.70. Just that way, you guys can get all the incentives.
stewart_read: The DQ itself is correct and unavoidable given the stated 530 score, but the close offers no concrete next step — no note to follow up when credit improves, no callback date, no referral resource for credit repair. The call simply ends.
alternative_hypothesis: Given this is a hard DQ with no schema-defined re-engagement path, ending the call here may be the only available procedural move, making this a scope-appropriate close rather than a rep failure.
coaching_implication: Discuss with the rep whether Ion has any standard practice for flagging DQ'd-on-credit leads for a future check-in (e.g., 6-12 months out) — if so, the rep should have offered it here instead of a flat close.
